Sleep paralysis is a supposed consequence of spiritual vulnerability in folk belief, rather than the meaning of the expression itself.

flags.why: The translation omits the stated cause and collapses 'yếu bóng vía' into 'bị bóng đè'.
flags.fix: I have a weak spirit, so I often experience sleep paralysis.

flags.why: Á khẩu means being unable to speak generally, rather than specifically having aphasia, as the [dictionary definition](https://vietnamthuquan.eu/TacPham/tu-dien-tieng-viet-1713/chuong-1) confirms.

Á khôi includes both first and second runners-up, as illustrated by [this contestant's account](https://tienphong.vn/nu-sinh-ngoai-thuong-tai-sac-ven-toan-la-a-khoi-2-cuoc-thi-hoa-khoi-sinh-vien-mien-bac-post1600178.tpo).
flags.fix: female runner-up in a beauty contest

flags.why: The Vietnamese example does not specify that she was the first runner-up.
flags.fix: She won a runner-up title in the contest.

flags.why: Á thánh denotes a blessed person or that person's rank, whereas beatification is the act of conferring the rank, as explained by [this Catholic source](https://hvanphongso.edu.vn/chi-tiet/chan-phuoc-va-hien-thanh).
flags.fix: a blessed person; the rank of Blessed (Catholic)
